analysis: The trial completed successfully but reduced host macro validation HR@10 to 0.4638, down 0.0137 from 0.4775 and 0.0412 from the 0.505 baseline. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.485, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.525, Electronics 0.380, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.465. Electronics improved from the previously reported 0.305 but remained below its 0.420 baseline; the aggregate result does not support this readout replacement. Candidate-conditioned attention increased expressiveness without improving overall ranking. Possible explanations include harder optimization or overfitting from candidate-dependent representations, but these metrics do not establish a cause. The supplied result reports 1169.06 allocated GPU-seconds. No hidden-test conclusions are available.
code_summary: Trained one independent model per category, deploying exactly one selected checkpoint for each route. Each model uses tied input/output item embeddings, a two-block causal Transformer backbone (128 dimensions, four heads), and two candidate-conditioned history attention heads with 32-dimensional queries/keys and learned log-age decay. Two pooled history summaries, the last contextual state, and the candidate embedding feed a 4×dimension MLP; normalized representations score candidates through the shared embedding, learned scale, and jointly trained item bias. Candidate scoring uses differentiable chunks of 16. Training retains prefix sampling, 64 uniform negatives with collision masks, binary logistic loss, AdamW, and validation HR@10 checkpoint selection. The predictor reconstructs the architecture and strictly loads one checkpoint per category; diagnostics cover finite gradients, causal masking, chunk equivalence, and reload parity. No ensembles or separately fitted auxiliary scorers are used.
